o: Heavenly Father, I thank You for this new day and for the breath of life You have given me. Before the tasks claim me, I want to pause a moment and place myself in Your presence. You know the road I will travel today, the places I will be and the people I will meet. Nothing that happens today surprises You, and that is why I rest in You.

Lord, sometimes my plans are many and my vision is short. Today I give You my projects, my decisions and my worries. Direct my steps, as Your Word says, and teach me to listen to Your voice when You point to a direction different from the one I had thought. Give me the courage to move forward when the road seems unknown and the humility to ask for help when I need it. May fear not stop me and may doubt not paralyze me.

I pray that You use me today to bless those around me. May my words be kind, my hands willing to serve and my heart attentive to the needs of others. Keep my family, protect those I love and accompany those going through difficult times today. Thank You, because Your faithfulness is new every morning and because You never let go of me. Help me walk by faith and believe that You go before me. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: On this day, November 16, 1855, the Scottish missionary and explorer David Livingstone beheld for the first time one of the most impressive natural wonders of Africa. He was traveling into the interior of the continent, on a long crossing, accompanied by local guides. The inhabitants of those lands called the cataract Mosi-oa-Tunya, which means “the smoke that thunders,” because of the column of vapor that rises and can be seen from afar.

Livingstone was a physician and had come to Africa as a missionary. His desire was to bring the message of the Gospel to peoples who had never heard it and to travel roads that others did not dare to take. Seeing this great waterfall, he named it Victoria, in honor of the queen of his country, and history remembers him as the first European to have beheld it.

This discovery was not the fruit of a comfortable stroll. The road demanded patience, illnesses to endure, rivers to cross and long distances far from his family and homeland. Livingstone advanced step by step, and each step brought him closer to what he did not yet know. His life reminds us that whoever dares to set out with a purpose, trusting in God, ends up seeing things he would not have seen by staying still.

The Bible teaches that a man's heart plans his way, but the LORD directs his steps. The disciples experienced this when Jesus asked them to go out into deep water, after a whole night of catching nothing. They obeyed, and the net nearly broke because of so many fish.
m: There are mornings when the day seems like a road without a map. We do not know what calls will come, what problems will arise or whether we will manage to finish what we have started. The story of Livingstone and that of Simon Peter teach us the same thing: God guides those who set out with trust.

The proverb says we may plan our way, and that is fine. God does not ask us to live without plans, but to place them in his hands. He is the one who directs the steps, and sometimes he does so by changing the route we had drawn. What matters is to keep a heart willing to be corrected and to follow his direction.

Peter was a fisherman by trade and knew that, in the daytime and after a night of failure, fishing made no sense. Yet he said: “At your word I will let down the nets.” This sentence is a great lesson for today. Obeying God when reason says it is useless opens doors we would never have imagined. The small obedience of one morning can change a whole life.

Apply this today in a simple way. Before going out, write down or think of a decision you have pending and present it to God in prayer. Then take a concrete step, even a small one: make that call, begin that task, ask forgiveness or help someone. During the day, ask calmly: “Lord, where do you want me to go now?” And when night comes, observe how he has accompanied you. God does not promise that we will see the whole road at once, but that he will go before us step by step.
m.c: Go out today with your head held high, for the Lord walks with you and takes care of every step you will take. May his peace accompany you in every decision and his grace sustain you when the road grows long. May God bless you and keep you this day.

o: Lord God, at the end of this day, I come before You with a grateful heart. Thank You for today's sustenance, for the people You placed on my path, for the strength You gave me and for every little blessing I may not have noticed while running here and there. Everything good comes from Your hand, and today I want to acknowledge it.

I now give You the prayers still awaiting an answer. You know how long I have been asking, and You also know the weariness of waiting. Teach me to believe that Your times are perfect and that You do not forget me. Take from my heart bitterness and haste, and fill it with hope. Forgive me for the times I doubted Your goodness, and for the moments I wanted to settle things by myself.

Grant me now deep rest. I lay at Your feet the burdens of the day, the worries of tomorrow and everything I could not settle. Take care of my family while we sleep, protect our homes and console those who weep tonight. When I wake, may my soul be renewed and ready to serve You. Thank You, because You always listen to me. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: Zechariah was an elderly priest who lived in the time of King Herod. He and his wife Elizabeth were righteous before God and walked blamelessly in his commandments. But they had a very great sorrow: Elizabeth had not been able to have children, and now both were advanced in years. For years, they had prayed, and the answer seemed not to come.

One day, it fell to Zechariah by lot to enter the sanctuary of the Lord to burn incense, while the people prayed outside. Suddenly, at the right side of the altar, an angel of the Lord appeared to him. Zechariah was troubled and fear fell upon him. But the angel said to him: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard.”

That prayer that seemed forgotten had been heard from the beginning. The angel announced that Elizabeth would bear a son, who would be named John, and that he would be a joy and delight to many. This child would later be the one who prepared the way for the Lord Jesus.

Zechariah had difficulty believing, and so he remained mute until the child's birth. Yet God's promise was fulfilled just as it had been spoken. This story teaches us that waiting does not mean abandonment. God listens, keeps every prayer and answers at the moment he knows to be best, very often when we no longer expect it.
m: When the day ends, many hearts are left thinking about what has not yet arrived: a healing, a job, the reconciliation of a family, an answer. The proverb describes it truthfully: hope deferred makes the heart sick. God does not mock this pain; he understands it.

The story of Zechariah reminds us that heaven did not ignore his prayer. For years it seemed that nothing was happening, but God was preparing something greater than what he had asked for. He would not receive only a son; he would be the father of the one who would announce the coming of the Savior. Sometimes the delay is the time in which God prepares a bigger plan.

The same proverb adds that a desire fulfilled is a tree of life. When God answers, he brings freshness, joy and new strength. But while the answer is on its way, he does not leave us alone. He sustains us by his presence, by his Word and by his peace. To wait in faith is not to stand with arms crossed, but to keep loving, serving and praying with trust.

Tonight, do something practical. Write on a piece of paper a prayer still awaiting an answer and give it to God in simple words. Then give thanks for one thing you have already received today. This trains the heart to wait with gratitude rather than with anguish. Tell the Lord: “I trust in your timing.” Then rest, for the one who keeps your prayers neither slumbers nor sleeps, and his faithfulness does not fail.
t.c: End this day with a grateful heart, for God has heard your words and keeps each one of your hopes. Leave in his hands what you could not change and receive his rest. May the Lord give you quiet sleep and a dawn full of peace.
